title: T‑Mobile Teams Restore Connectivity and Provide Community Support as Gulf Coast Communities Recover from Hurricane Isaias (Updated 10/15)
summary: With nearly all T‑Mobile cell sites operational following Hurricane Isaias, our teams continue providing connectivity and community support as utility crews work to restore power across the Gulf Coast

# **Update: October 12, 2026 | More Than 99% of T‑Mobile Cell Sites Operational Across Hurricane Isaias-Impacted Areas as Community Support Expands**


Our hearts are with the families and communities across the Gulf Coast recovering from Hurricane Isaias. We know how much staying connected matters right now, whether it’s reaching loved ones, checking on neighbors or getting help. T‑Mobile crews continue making progress restoring service, supporting first responders and bringing additional connectivity resources to affected communities.


### **Network Restoration**


More than 99% of T‑Mobile’s macro cell sites were operational across the areas impacted by Hurricane Isaias, as of Sunday afternoon. With the vast majority of sites operational, our crews continue working around the clock to address remaining impacts, largely caused by widespread commercial power disruptions.


T-Satellite has provided an additional way to stay connected in areas where traditional cellular service wasn’t available. Since the start of the event, 156,000 text messages have been sent and received via satellite. Our Self-Organizing Network (SON) technology has continued adapting to changing conditions, automatically adjusting neighboring cell sites to help maintain coverage and keep people connected.


### **Free Wi-Fi, Charging and Supplies**


Our teams are providing resources across the Florida Panhandle where all community members, regardless of their wireless provider, can stop by to access free Wi-Fi and charge their devices. Power packs containing a portable power bank and charging supplies will also be available at select locations, while supplies last.


- **T‑Mobile Gulf Breeze Store:** 3781 Gulf Breeze Pkwy, Gulf Breeze, FL 32563. Free Wi-Fi, device charging and power-pack distribution available **Monday, October 12, from 10 a.m. to 4 p.m. CT** , while supplies last.
- **Morgan Sports Complex, Destin Storm Recovery Insurance Village:** 4200 Indian Bayou Trail, Destin, FL 32541. Free Wi-Fi, device charging and power-pack distribution available **Monday, October 12, from 10 a.m. to 4 p.m. CT** , while supplies last.
- **T‑Mobile Destin Experience Store:** 4291 Legendary Dr., Suite J119, Destin, FL 32541. Free Wi-Fi and device charging available **24/7** .


Our teams also distributed 50 power packs to community members in Pensacola on Sunday. As recovery continues, we’ll keep bringing support where it’s needed most. Community support locations and hours may shift as needs evolve, and we’ll share updates on where resources are available, including any new locations as they’re confirmed.


### **Supporting First Responders and Emergency Operations**


We’re continuing to work directly with public safety agencies to address critical connectivity needs, deploying network restoration resources and additional connectivity solutions where needed. Among those efforts, our teams have helped agencies in Geneva and Mobile County, Alabama, support their emergency response operations. In Florida, a satellite-equipped mobile cell site (SatCOLT) is now providing connectivity at the Walton County Emergency Operations Center.


As communities continue the difficult work of recovery, we’re grateful to the crews, first responders and local partners helping people through it.

# **PM Update: October 10, 2026** | **A Message from Jon Freier**


As Gulf Coast communities begin the difficult work of recovery, our hearts are with everyone impacted by Hurricane Isaias, and we’re grateful to the teams working tirelessly to help. T‑Mobile Chief Operating Officer[Jon Freier shared a message](https://lnkd.in/p/g5MMVVMV) recognizing their efforts to restore connectivity and support affected communities, reaffirming our commitment to being there throughout recovery.


###


---


**BELLEVUE, Wash. — October 10, 2026** — Across the Gulf Coast, families and communities are facing the aftermath of Hurricane Isaias, including the tragic loss of life, damaged homes, flooding and widespread power outages. Our hearts are with those who have lost loved ones and everyone affected by the storm. At a time when reaching family, checking on neighbors or getting help matters more than ever, staying connected is especially important.


**KEY UPDATES**


- **Maintaining connectivity and restoring service** : Approximately 96% of T‑Mobile sites across the affected area are operational as of Saturday morning, despite widespread power outages. Teams worked to restore connectivity to the vast majority of customers within hours of Isaias impacting communities. Our[Self-Organizing Network (SON)](https://tmobile-newsroom.wistia.com/medias/mo96mmphvr) technology has made more than 7,500 automated adjustments since October 9, helping neighboring cell sites adapt to changing conditions and maintain coverage as restoration continues. Crews are deploying generators, refueling equipment and prioritizing restoration in the hardest-hit areas as quickly and safely as possible.
- **T-Satellite helping people stay connected** : On Friday, October 9, more than 16,000 people used[T-Satellite](https://www.t-mobile.com/coverage/satellite-phone-service) to send and receive over 38,000 text messages, providing another way to communicate when traditional cellular coverage isn’t available.
- **Supporting first responders with T-Priority** : T‑Mobile is coordinating with emergency management agencies to prioritize restoration in hard-hit communities, including deploying mobile assets to the Geneva, Alabama, area. Eligible first responders and public safety agencies can receive 30 days of[T-Priority](https://www.t-mobile.com/t-priority) with T-Satellite at no charge to support critical communications.
- **Helping communities through recovery** : Teams are arriving in affected areas with Wi-Fi and device-charging resources, while T‑Mobile is putting additional customer relief measures in place, including **unlimited talk, text and data** for customers, and providing support to employees impacted by the storm. See below for details.
- **See below for additional updates shared on October 7 and October 9.**


-
-
- T‑Mobile SatCOLT Deployment to Walton Co, Florida, October 2026


T‑Mobile crews are already making progress restoring connectivity following the hurricane’s landfall near Destin, Florida, Friday night. Commercial power outages are responsible for the vast majority of network disruptions, particularly in the Mobile, Alabama, area. Our network’s built-in resiliency and backup power systems are helping keep most sites operating despite widespread power loss.


“Our thoughts are with the families who have lost loved ones and everyone impacted by Hurricane Isaias,” said Ankur Kapoor, Chief Network Officer, T‑Mobile. “Keeping people connected is one way T‑Mobile can help communities through this difficult time. Our network has held strong despite widespread commercial power outages, with intelligent technology making automatic network adjustments to help maintain coverage. Our crews are working to restore service where it’s been impacted, while T-Satellite provides another way to reach family and friends, and T-Priority supports first responders’ critical communications. We’re committed to doing everything we can for the communities counting on us throughout recovery.”


As of Saturday morning, more than 96% of our sites were operational across the four affected markets. Overlapping coverage from neighboring sites is helping some customers stay connected even where individual sites are affected. Restoration is underway, with crews deploying generators, refueling equipment and prioritizing critical communications needs to bring service back as quickly and safely as possible.


**Our network technology is also helping people stay connected as restoration continues:**


- **Making thousands of real-time network adjustments:** Our[Self-Organizing Network (SON)](https://tmobile-newsroom.wistia.com/medias/mo96mmphvr) technology has been working throughout the storm, automatically adapting network performance as individual sites are affected. Since October 9, SON has made more than 7,500 automated adjustments across cell sites, helping neighboring sites respond to changing conditions and maintain coverage wherever possible.
- **Providing another way to stay connected:**[T-Satellite](https://www.t-mobile.com/coverage/satellite-phone-service) , opened up to all customers with compatible phones ahead of the storm, is providing an additional connection option when traditional cellular coverage isn’t available. People can text loved ones, let family know they’re safe or reach emergency services through Text to 911 via satellite. On Friday, October 9 alone, more than 16,000 unique users sent and received more than 38,000 text messages through T-Satellite. Behind those numbers are people finding another way to reach loved ones, let family know they’re safe or stay connected during an uncertain time.


**On the ground, our teams are responding to the needs of affected communities:**


- **Restoring service and prioritizing critical communications:** Crews are deploying additional generators, refueling sites and addressing power and equipment issues to bring connectivity back online. We’re also working closely with emergency management agencies and first responders to identify where service is needed most, particularly in hard-hit communities around Mobile, and prioritize restoration accordingly. Mobile assets are being deployed in coordination with public safety partners to help address critical coverage needs in the Geneva, Alabama, area.
- **Bringing support to communities:** Our teams are arriving in affected areas Saturday with vehicles and Wi-Fi equipment to help people stay connected and charge their devices. Teams are coordinating with local partners to identify where support is needed most, including shelters, community gathering locations and potentially T‑Mobile stores. We’ll share more details as locations and services are confirmed.
- **Helping customers stay connected through recovery:** T‑Mobile is providing unlimited talk, text and data to eligible T‑Mobile, Metro by T‑Mobile, Assurance Wireless, Mint Mobile and Ultra Mobile customers in impacted areas who don’t already have these benefits included in their plans from Saturday October 10 through Friday, October 16. This includes customers with billing zip codes in the following Alabama and Florida counties:


- **Taking care of employees:** We’re checking on employees impacted by the storm and providing additional assistance, including temporary lodging when needed, to help them and their families through this difficult time.
- **Helping customers navigate store closures:** Some T‑Mobile stores remain closed due to storm-related power outages, while others are being assessed for reopening as conditions improve. Customers should check the[T‑Mobile store locator](https://www.t-mobile.com/stores/locator) and call ahead before visiting.


Our teams will continue working to restore connectivity, support first responders and stand alongside affected communities throughout recovery. Because every connection matters, especially when people need each other most.

For more information on T‑Mobile’s preparedness and response capabilities, visit the company’s[Emergency Response hub](https://www.t-mobile.com/news/emergency-response) and follow @TMobileNews on X and Instagram.

# **October 9, 2026: T‑Mobile Activates T-Satellite, Mobilizes Resources Ahead of Hurricane Isaias**


*As the tropical system strengthens in the Gulf, T‑Mobile is preparing for potential impacts and sharing simple steps families can take now to stay connected and ready*


As Hurricane Isaias, now a Category 3 storm, approaches the northern Gulf Coast, evacuation orders are already in place in some communities as families and businesses prepare for dangerous winds, flooding and potential commercial power outages. Staying connected to loved ones, emergency services, and critical information can make all the difference. That’s why T‑Mobile is taking additional steps now — activating T-Satellite and moving network equipment, personnel and support resources closer to communities in the storm’s path.


**Here’s how T‑Mobile is preparing and responding:**


- **Helping people stay connected when it matters most:** T‑Mobile has opened up[T-Satellite](https://www.t-mobile.com/coverage/satellite-phone-service) ahead of Hurricane Isaias, extending satellite texting to all members with compatible devices in the affected area. If traditional cellular coverage is disrupted, customers may still have a way to text loved ones, let family know they’re safe or reach out for help via Text to 911 over satellite. T-Satellite also supports Wireless Emergency Alerts, giving people another way to receive critical information — even if they’re not T‑Mobile customers.
- **Strengthening network readiness** : Our teams have moved additional portable generators closer to the anticipated impact area, with crews, fuel supplies and mobile[network assets](https://www.t-mobile.com/news/disaster-definitions) , including SatCOLTs, positioned to support restoration when conditions are safe. We’re also using our Self-Organizing Network (SON) technology to help optimize network performance as conditions change, while satellite-backhaul equipment provides another option to restore connectivity if traditional network connections are disrupted. We also have access to boats and high-water vehicles to reach areas affected by flooding, as well as heavy-lift drones capable of delivering smaller critical supplies if needed. Together, these preparations help our teams respond and restore service as safely and quickly as conditions allow.
- **Supporting first responders:** We’re working closely with state emergency management agencies, Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) and Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) to identify critical communications needs and priority locations. For eligible first responders and public safety agencies, we can coordinate 30 days of[T-Priority](https://www.t-mobile.com/t-priority) with T-Satellite at no charge through eSIM activation on compatible, unlocked devices. Loaner devices are also available for agencies that need them.
- **Mobilizing community support:** As emergency shelters open across the region, we’re preparing to deploy community support teams with vehicles and Wi-Fi equipment to provide connectivity and charging support where needed, as conditions allow. Whether it’s reaching a loved one, checking on family or accessing important updates, having a way to connect can bring peace of mind during an uncertain time.
- **Supporting customers and employees:** We’re proactively closing stores in areas facing severe weather to put employee and customer safety first. Before visiting a store, customers should check the[T‑Mobile store locator](https://www.t-mobile.com/stores/locator) for nearby locations and hours and call ahead when possible.


Our teams will continue monitoring conditions, working with emergency management partners and positioning resources to respond as soon as it’s safe. We’re committed to doing everything we can to help customers, first responders and communities stay connected through the storm and its aftermath.


**For those in the storm’s path:** Please follow local emergency officials for evacuation and safety guidance, keep devices and backup batteries charged, and review your family emergency plan. Our preparedness resources below offer additional steps to help you and the people you care about stay connected and ready.

# **October 7, 2026: T‑Mobile Helps Gulf Coast Communities Prepare as Tropical Storm Isaias Strengthens**


When a hurricane is possible, preparing before conditions worsen can help families stay safer, more informed and connected.


According to the National Hurricane Center (NHC), Tropical Storm Isaias has formed in the Gulf and is forecast to rapidly strengthen, becoming a hurricane by Thursday as it turns northeast and north toward the northern Gulf Coast later this week. While uncertainty remains around its exact track, intensity and impacts, the NHC says there is an increasing risk of dangerous wind and storm surge impacts along portions of the northern Gulf Coast and urges residents from Louisiana to the Florida Panhandle to monitor the forecast and make sure their hurricane plans are in place.


### **T‑Mobile is taking steps to prepare**


Our teams are topping off generators, readying equipment and positioning resources ahead of potential impacts. We’re also using advanced network technology, including[Self-Organizing Network (SON)](https://tmobile-newsroom.wistia.com/medias/mo96mmphvr) capabilities, to help optimize network performance as conditions change. AI-powered Dynamic CX is another tool available to our teams to help anticipate changing network needs and adjust capacity as conditions evolve.


At the same time, we’re working directly with public safety and emergency management partners across the Gulf Coast to identify anticipated communications needs and priority locations.


Eligible first responders and agencies can receive 30 days of[T-Priority](https://www.t-mobile.com/T-Priority?msockid=0810e24aa91a6d702536f4b6a8c36c54) at no charge through a secondary SIM or eSIM on a compatible, unlocked device, or through loaner devices. T-Priority provides prioritized connectivity on T‑Mobile’s network during times of congestion, including[satellite connectivity](https://www.t-mobile.com/coverage/satellite-phone-service?msockid=0810e24aa91a6d702536f4b6a8c36c54) that adds another way to stay connected when terrestrial coverage is unavailable.


As the forecast evolves, we’re prepared to deploy additional portable generators,[mobile network assets](https://www.t-mobile.com/news/disaster-definitions) including SatCOLTs (Satellite Cell on Light Trucks) and drones, and community support trucks and trailers where they may be needed to help keep customers, first responders and communities connected.


And while our teams prepare, there are simple steps you can take now to help make sure you and the people you care about are ready, too.


### **Get Your Tech Storm-Ready**


Take a few minutes to prepare the technology that can help you stay connected and informed. Charge phones, tablets and backup batteries. Enable emergency alerts and download important information you may need if connectivity is disrupted. Keep charging cables and portable power banks with your emergency supplies, and protect devices from water and other potential damage.


Tips from T‑Mobile to Stay safe, prepared and connected


During an emergency, always follow instructions and evacuation guidance from local authorities.


### **Make a Plan for the People Who Matter Most**


Preparedness isn’t just about supplies. It’s also knowing what your family will do if plans suddenly change.


Where will you meet if you’re separated? How will you reach one another? Who is your out-of-area contact? What will you do if you need to evacuate? Does your plan account for medications, accessibility needs, children, older family members and pets?


Our Family Emergency Plan can help you put those answers in one place so everyone knows what to do and where to find important information.


Click on ‘Download Media Assets’ above and take a few minutes to fill it out together, then make sure everyone has access to a copy.
